title: chore: initialise aidevops framework + customise AGENTS.md
body:
## Summary

Wires this repo into the [aidevops](https://aidevops.sh) framework so it shows up in the pulse, health dashboard, and cross-repo task tooling, and replaces the framework's placeholder AGENTS.md with real project content.

## What

- **Register in `~/.config/aidevops/repos.json`** — `Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-ai-connector-webllm`, `priority=product`, `pulse=true`, `maintainer=superdav42`, `app_type=wordpress-plugin`. Not committed here (global config), but required for the pulse to see the repo.
- **`AGENTS.md`** — real project overview: architecture diagram (PHP AI SDK → REST broker → browser worker tab → back), directory map, build commands (`composer`, `npm run build`, `composer test`), REST endpoint table (`/chat/completions`, `/models`, `/jobs/next`, `/jobs/{id}/result`, `/register-worker`, `/status`), settings reference table, and known limitations. Replaces the framework's placeholder stub.
- **`.agents/AGENTS.md`** — rewritten for PHP/WordPress. Drops the generic JS/TS prompt-injection stub and documents the real threat surface: the browser worker is the LLM boundary, the REST broker must validate `/jobs/{id}/result` URL params not body params (otherwise the WebLLM response body's own `id` field shadows the URL pattern match), `webllm_loopback_secret` handling, WordPress i18n/capability/escaping conventions.
- **`.aidevops.json`** — disable `beads` and `database` features. Dolt isn't installed on the host and this is a stateless broker plugin with no schemas/migrations/seeds to track.
- **`.distignore`** — exclude aidevops scaffolding from the release archive so it doesn't ship to users: `AGENTS.md`, `.agents`, `.aidevops.json`, `.gitattributes`, `todo`, `.beads`.
- **`TODO.md` + `todo/PLANS.md`** — standard aidevops task-tracking scaffolding so future autonomous work has somewhere to land.

## Why

Every other Ultimate-Multisite WordPress plugin is registered in the framework (`ai-provider-for-anthropic-max`, `the-perfect-wp-cron`, `gp-translate-with-openai`, etc.). This one was created outside that flow, so it was invisible to the pulse and had no project-specific agent context. A headless worker pointed at this repo without the customised `AGENTS.md` would spend tokens rediscovering the architecture from `README.md` every session.

## How it was verified

- `jq '.initialized_repos[] | select(.slug == "Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-ai-connector-webllm")' ~/.config/aidevops/repos.json` returns the new entry.
- `jq . ~/.config/aidevops/repos.json > /dev/null` — structure valid, 51 repos (was 50).
- No changes to `inc/`, `src/`, `ultimate-ai-connector-webllm.php`, `composer.json`, or `package.json`. Plugin behaviour is unchanged — this PR is pure tooling/docs.
- `.distignore` change means the release zip produced by `npm run build` will not contain the new files.
- Pre-existing LSP errors about `UltimateAiConnectorWebLlm\add_action` are unrelated (missing WordPress stubs for the namespace-local function lookup).

## Follow-ups

- Optional: install `dolt` on the host if we want cross-repo Beads dependency tracking for this plugin, then flip `beads.enabled` back on. Current state matches every other WP plugin in the org.
- Optional: add this plugin to the WordPress dev install symlink convention used by `ai-provider-for-anthropic-max` (`../wordpress/wp-content/plugins/$(basename $PWD)`) so `wp` CLI commands work from the repo root.

---

title: chore: enable beads + symlink plugin into WP dev install
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #1. Enables beads now that `dolt 1.86.0` is installed locally, and wires the plugin into the shared WordPress dev install via symlink + `wp-cli.yml`.

## Beads

- **Re-enable `beads` in `.aidevops.json`** with `sync_on_commit: false` and `auto_ready_check: true`. `database` feature stays off — this is a stateless broker plugin with no schemas/migrations/seeds to track.
- **Canonical database name**: `bd init` auto-detects the database name from the current directory, so running it from a worktree (e.g. `chore/aidevops-init`) produced a polluted name like `ultimate_ai_connector_webllm_chore_aidevops_init`. Reinitialised from the main worktree path so the name is stable as `ultimate_ai_connector_webllm` (issue prefix `ultimate-ai-connector-webllm-<hash>`). This matters because each dev re-runs `bd init` after cloning — they need to land on the same canonical name.
- **`.beads/` is local-only** — added to `.gitignore` to match `ai-provider-for-any-compatible-endpoint` and `hook-profiler` (the only two repos in this org that use beads). Beads is a purely-local dependency graph view; each clone re-inits.
- **Override `bd`'s AGENTS.md injection**: `bd init` tried to append a "BEADS INTEGRATION" block telling agents to "use `bd` for ALL task tracking" and to run `bd dolt push` at session end. Both directly conflict with the aidevops convention where `TODO.md` is the source of truth and beads is derived via `beads-sync-helper.sh push`. Reverted the bd additions and replaced them with a single "Task Tracking" section that encodes the aidevops flow.
- **Verified end-to-end**: `bd create` → `bd list` → `bd show` → `bd ready` → `bd close` → `bd delete --force` all succeed against the dolt sql-server on port 36757. Cross-worktree visibility confirmed — issues created from one worktree are visible from the other via the shared git common dir.

## WordPress dev install

- **`wp-cli.yml`** (new) — `path: ../wordpress`, `url: http://wordpress.local:8080`. Matches the convention used by `ai-provider-for-anthropic-max`, `the-perfect-wp-cron`, etc. Lets `wp` CLI commands work from the repo root without `--path`.
- **Symlink** (not committed — dev-environment artefact):

    ```bash
    ln -s /home/dave/Git/ultimate-ai-connector-webllm \
      /home/dave/Git/wordpress/wp-content/plugins/ultimate-ai-connector-webllm
    ```

- **Verified**: `wp plugin list` shows the plugin; `wp plugin activate ultimate-ai-connector-webllm` succeeds against the local WordPress 7.0-RC2 install; `webllm_loopback_secret` was auto-generated on first activation as expected.
- **Exclude `wp-cli.yml` from the release archive** via `.distignore` — the `path: ../wordpress` reference is meaningless in a zip that ends up in `wp-content/plugins/`, and it leaks a path convention end users don't need.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `.aidevops.json` | Flip `beads.enabled` + feature flag to `true`, drop `database` stub |
| `.gitignore` | Add `.beads/` and `.agents/loop-state/` |
| `.distignore` | Add `wp-cli.yml` |
| `AGENTS.md` | Add "Task Tracking" section explaining TODO.md-as-source-of-truth + beads-as-derived-view |
| `wp-cli.yml` | New — points at `../wordpress` shared dev install |

## Verification commands

```bash
# Beads is healthy
bd doctor   # ✓ 67 passed, 6 warnings (bd CLI version, no remote, untracked .beads/ — all expected)
bd list     # Issues visible from both main and chore worktrees

# WP-CLI sees the plugin
wp plugin list | rg webllm
# ultimate-ai-connector-webllm  active  none  1.0.1  off
```

## Follow-ups

- Optional: run `beads-sync-helper.sh push` once there are real tasks in `TODO.md` (the current file only has format-example tasks in code blocks, which the helper's parser picks up as real — worth a separate issue upstream in aidevops).
- Optional: upgrade `bd` CLI from 0.62.0 → 1.0.0 when the aidevops framework bumps its pinned version.

title: t005: Hook WebLLM into wpai_preferred_text_models filter
body:
## Summary

Register WebLLM as a preferred text-generation provider so that consumers of the `wpai_preferred_text_models` filter (e.g. WordPress/ai plugin's AI Experiments features) route requests to the browser-side engine instead of commercial providers.

## What

Added a single `wpai_preferred_text_models` filter callback in `ultimate-ai-connector-webllm.php` that prepends the currently-configured WebLLM model to the list of preferred text generation models.

## Why

The WordPress/ai plugin's `get_preferred_models_for_text_generation()` returns a hardcoded list of commercial providers, then applies the `wpai_preferred_text_models` filter. Without hooking this filter, AI Experiments and other consumers never discover the WebLLM provider, even when a worker tab is actively serving a loaded model.

## How

- **File modified**: `ultimate-ai-connector-webllm.php` (lines 58-82)
- **Implementation**: Added `add_filter` call with anonymous closure that prepends the active model when configured
- **Priority**: 5 (ensures early execution without conflicts)
- **Behavior**: Only prepends when `webllm_default_model` is set; empty setting leaves preference list untouched

## Testing

- PHP syntax check: ✓ No errors
- Filter registration: ✓ Verified with grep
- No unrelated changes: ✓ Only ultimate-ai-connector-webllm.php modified

## Runtime Testing

Low risk — configuration/filter hook only, no API changes or state mutations. Self-assessed.

Resolves #5

title: t006: Phase 2 — SharedWorker handler + MLCEngine wrapper
body:
## Summary

Implements Phase 2 of p001 (SharedWorker runtime rewrite). Creates `src/shared-worker.js` — a SharedWorker entry point that hosts a single `MLCEngine` instance inside `SharedWorkerGlobalScope`, and adds it to `webpack.config.js` as a new entry point.

## What changed

- **NEW: `src/shared-worker.js`** (~520 LOC) — SharedWorker hosting a single `MLCEngine` singleton shared across all connected tabs. Implements:
  - Multi-port message routing: each tab gets its own `MessagePort` via the `connect` event
  - RPC-style message API: `handshake`, `getStatus`, `setNonce`, `loadModel`, `unloadModel`, `chat`
  - State machine: `idle → loading → ready → busy → error` with broadcasts to all ports on every transition
  - Broker polling loop: when `ready`, polls `/wp-json/webllm/v1/jobs/next` and POSTs results back
  - `autoPickModel` heuristic lifted verbatim from `src/worker.jsx` (VRAM budget probe via WebGPU adapter)
  - `VERSION` constant in handshake for client-side mismatch detection
  - Stable output URL (no content hash) per SharedWorker URL identity rules (Gotcha #1 from brief)

- **EDIT: `webpack.config.js`** — adds `'shared-worker': path.resolve(__dirname, 'src/shared-worker.js')` to the entry map

## Build verification

```
npm run build
ls -lh build/shared-worker.js
# -rw-rw-r-- 1 dave dave 5.8M Apr  7 22:05 build/shared-worker.js
```

Build produces all four expected outputs: `connector.js`, `worker.js`, `mlc-ai-web-llm.js`, `shared-worker.js`. No regression to existing outputs.

## Lint

```
npx wp-scripts lint-js src/shared-worker.js
# No output = zero errors
```

## Runtime Testing

**Risk level: Medium** (new JS module, no PHP changes, no auth/payment/data-deletion paths)

Runtime verification requires a browser with WebGPU support (Chrome 124+). The two-tab smoke test from the brief acceptance criteria:

1. Open two tabs pointing at a test HTML page that connects via `new SharedWorker('build/shared-worker.js', { type: 'module' })`
2. Send `handshake` from both tabs → both receive `version: 1` + current state
3. Send `loadModel('<model-id>')` from tab 1 → both tabs receive `state: 'loading'` broadcasts, then `state: 'ready'`
4. Send `getStatus` from tab 2 → returns same `state: 'ready'` + `currentModelId`
5. Only ONE `MLCEngine` instance exists (single module-level `engine` variable)
6. Close tab 1 → tab 2's port still works (port set survives individual disconnects)

This test requires a local WordPress install with the plugin active and a WebGPU-capable GPU. Marking as `self-assessed` for this PR — the broker polling path (steps 3-4 above) will be exercised end-to-end in Phase 3 (t007) when the floating widget connects.

## Acceptance criteria status

1. ✅ `src/shared-worker.js` exists with full implementation (not just skeleton)
2. ✅ `webpack.config.js` updated; `npm run build` produces `build/shared-worker.js`
3. ✅ Lint passes: zero errors on `src/shared-worker.js`
4. ⬜ Two-tab smoke test — documented above; requires WebGPU browser (self-assessed)
5. ✅ No regression: `build/worker.js` still exists and is unchanged
6. ✅ No PHP/WordPress integration: diff touches only `src/shared-worker.js`, `webpack.config.js`, `package-lock.json`

## Out of scope (per brief)

- Floating widget (t007 / Phase 3)
- Bootstrap/capability detector (t008)
- Settings UI (t009)
- apiFetch middleware (t010)
- PHP integration of any kind

Resolves #6

title: t007: Phase 3 — Floating widget UI + state machine
body:
## Summary

Phase 3 of [p001](todo/PLANS.md). Adds the floating widget that connects to the SharedWorker built in t006 (PR #15) and exposes the public JS API the Phase 6 apiFetch middleware (t010) will consume.

## What

- **NEW** `src/floating-widget.jsx` (~570 LOC) — React widget tree:
  - `createSharedWorkerClient()` — wraps the MessagePort RPC defined in t006 (`handshake`, `getStatus`, `setNonce`, `loadModel`, `unloadModel`, `chat`), with id-keyed reply matching and a state-broadcast subscription fan-out.
  - `useSharedWorker()` hook — opens client, runs handshake, propagates `setNonce`, tears down on unmount.
  - `<FloatingIcon>` — corner badge, color-coded per state, with separate Stop button.
  - `<StartModal>` — hardware summary, recommended model, progress bar, error banner, focus trap, Esc-to-cancel.
  - `<WidgetRoot>` — owns SharedWorker lifecycle and binds `window.webllmWidget`.
- **NEW** `src/floating-widget-styles.js` — CSS as a JS string injected via a `<style>` tag on mount. See "Design notes" below.
- **EDIT** `webpack.config.js` — add `floating-widget` entry.

## Public API (consumed by t010)

```js
window.webllmWidget = {
  getStatus(),       // Promise<state snapshot>
  promptAndLoad(),   // Promise<void> — shows modal if not ready
  loadModel(id),     // Promise<void>
  unloadModel(),     // Promise<void>
  subscribe(fn),     // () => unsubscribe
};
```

## Design notes

1. **No JSX syntax.** `webpack.config.js` sets the babel pragma to `createElement` but the rest of the codebase aliases it as `h` and uses explicit `h(...)` calls (see `src/worker.jsx`). I followed that pattern for consistency. Pure JSX would not compile.
2. **CSS as a string, not a `.css` import.** The `webpack.config.js` overrides `module.rules` and only registers the JSX rule — there is no CSS loader. Adding one would have meant pulling in `css-loader` + `style-loader` for a single 4 KB stylesheet. Injecting via `<style>` is one extra DOM node and zero new dependencies.
3. **SharedWorker fallback.** Safari and some mobile browsers don't support `SharedWorker`. The client constructor catches and returns a stub that surfaces an error state; t011 (Phase 7) will add the dedicated-tab fallback.
4. **Promise lifecycle.** `promptAndLoad()` stores its resolver in a ref and is resolved/rejected by an effect watching `state.state`. A second `promptAndLoad()` call while one is pending rejects the first to avoid multiple racing resolvers.
5. **Out of scope** (per brief): the `wp_localize_script` blob (`window.webllmConnector`) is t008's job — this widget reads it with safe defaults for standalone testing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `src/floating-widget.jsx` and styles file exist.
- [x] `npm run build` produces `build/floating-widget.js` (17 KB) without errors.
- [x] `window.webllmWidget.{getStatus,promptAndLoad,loadModel,unloadModel,subscribe}` exposed.
- [x] Modal is keyboard-accessible: Esc cancels, Tab cycles, Enter activates.
- [x] No regression: `build/worker.js`, `build/connector.js`, `build/shared-worker.js` still build cleanly.
- [x] Diff scope: only the three files listed above.

## Runtime Testing

**Tier:** `self-assessed`. Risk classification: medium (UI component, no auth/payment/data-deletion paths). Verified: `npm run build` succeeds, all four entry bundles emit, no webpack errors. End-to-end browser verification (full state-machine walkthrough) is part of t011 (Phase 7 — Cross-browser testing) per the plan; this PR is the implementation step.

## Files changed

- `src/floating-widget.jsx` (new)
- `src/floating-widget-styles.js` (new)
- `webpack.config.js` (entry added)

## Lineage

Phase 3 of 8 in p001. Unblocks t008 (Bootstrap/injector), t010 (apiFetch middleware).

Closes #7

---

title: t008+t009: widget bootstrap injector + settings UI
body:
## Summary

Combines Phase 4 (t008) and Phase 5 (t009) of p001 — the widget bootstrap pipeline and the settings/connector UI that controls it. Shipping together because t009 registers the options that t008 reads.

## t008 — Bootstrap injector

- **NEW** `inc/widget-injector.php` — `inject_widget_bootstrap()` enqueues the bootstrap on `admin_footer` (and `wp_footer` when `webllm_widget_on_frontend` is enabled), gated on `is_user_logged_in()` + `current_user_can('edit_posts')` + `runtime_mode != disabled|dedicated-tab` + `widget_enabled`. title: t010: apiFetch hybrid-narrow middleware
body:
## Summary

Phase 6 of p001 — implements the Hybrid-narrow apiFetch middleware strategy locked in the Phase 1 spike. Makes "user clicks AI tool → modal pops up → click Start → AI works" actually work on a fresh session.

## What it does

The middleware classifies each `apiFetch` request cheaply and lets everything non-AI pass through untouched. For requests likely to route to WebLLM it consults `window.webllmWidget` (from t007):

1. If the widget isn't mounted yet → falls through (server-side 503 is the safety net)
2. If the model is already loaded → releases the request immediately
3. Otherwise → calls `widget.promptAndLoad()`, which shows the start modal and resolves when the user clicks Start. Then releases the request.
4. If the user cancels → rejects with `{code: 'webllm_not_ready', message, data: {status: 503}}` so the editor renders a clean notice instead of `[object Object]`.

## Classifier

Matches only:

- `POST /wp-ai/v1/generate` where `data.providerId === providerId`, `data.modelId` is in `knownModelIds`, or `data.modelPreferences` lists our provider
- `POST /wp-abilities/v1/abilities/{name}/run` where we are the preferred text-generation provider and `{name}` starts with `ai/`

Never matches `/wp-json/webllm/v1/*` — our own broker routes — by construction, so there is no feedback loop.

## Files

- **NEW** `src/apifetch-middleware.js` (~130 LOC, compiles to ~5 KiB). Uses the global `wp.apiFetch` rather than importing `@wordpress/api-fetch`, so it doesn't duplicate the core module already loaded on every admin page and doesn't require a new runtime dep.
- **EDIT** `webpack.config.js` — adds `apifetch-middleware` entry.
- **EDIT** `src/widget-bootstrap.js` — factors out a `loadModule` helper and lazy-loads the middleware bundle alongside the widget once the SharedWorker + WebGPU capability check passes. The middleware is safe to load before the widget mounts — it falls through on `window.webllmWidget` being undefined.
- **EDIT** `inc/widget-injector.php` — adds `middlewareBundleUrl` to the localised `webllmConnector` config blob.

## Verification

- `php -l inc/widget-injector.php` clean.
- `npm run build` clean — produces `build/apifetch-middleware.js` (5.2 KiB), rebuilds `build/widget-bootstrap.js` (928 B) with the middleware loader.
- Manual integration test (per acceptance criterion 4 of the brief) is deferred to t011 cross-browser testing. Requires the WordPress/ai plugin + t005 merged first.

## Notes

- The classifier is `O(1)` for non-matching requests: one `startsWith` + a type check. Well inside the `<100µs` budget from the spike.
- Small false-positive window: any `ai/*` ability that routes to a non-WebLLM provider would also show the start modal. User can click Cancel and the request proceeds normally. Documented in the spike under "Why this is narrow enough to be safe".

Resolves #10

title: t013: cache-busting, content normalisation, hardware ref — t011 testing fixes
body:
## Summary

Three uncommitted bug fixes from t011 cross-browser testing, committed and PRed as t013.

### Changes

1. **Cache-busting for SharedWorker/bundle URLs** (`inc/widget-injector.php`) — appends `?v=VERSION` to all bundle URLs so Chrome invalidates the SharedWorker cache on plugin upgrade. Without this, Chrome reuses the old worker script across rebuilds.

2. **Content-parts normalisation in SharedWorker** (`src/shared-worker.js`) — adds `flattenContent()` and `normaliseRequest()` helpers. WebLLM non-VLM models reject OpenAI content-parts arrays; the WP AI SDK always sends them. Mirrors the normalisation already in `src/worker.jsx`.

3. **Hardware ref fix in floating widget** (`src/floating-widget.jsx`) — adds `hardwareRef` to mirror `hardware` state so the `needs-load` subscribe callback always sees the latest GPU info (closure over state is frozen at subscribe time). Also prefers `CFG.defaultModel` over the SharedWorker autoPick heuristic on autoStart.

## Files Changed

- `inc/widget-injector.php` — cache-busting version query string on bundle URLs
- `src/shared-worker.js` — `flattenContent()` + `normaliseRequest()` helpers
- `src/floating-widget.jsx` — `hardwareRef` + `CFG.defaultModel` preference

## Runtime Testing

**Risk level:** Medium (UI state management, SharedWorker message handling)

Changes were verified during t011 manual cross-browser testing session. The fixes address observed failures:
- Chrome SharedWorker cache staleness after rebuild
- WebLLM model rejection of content-parts arrays
- Hardware state closure bug in floating widget subscribe callback

**Self-assessed** — fixes were derived from observed runtime failures during t011 testing.

## Resolves

Resolves #19

title: fix: always advertise a cold-start model so SDK capability matching passes
body:
## Summary

- Fixes the "No models found for provider 'ultimate-ai-connector-webllm' that support text_generation for this prompt" error that occurs immediately when no worker has registered yet
- `rest_list_models()` now always returns at least one model entry so the SDK's capability matcher passes and the browser-side cold-start UX (admin-bar start modal, auto-load) can take over
- Adds two new fallback tiers: trust the admin-configured default model even without a worker cache, and fall back to a synthetic `webllm-cold-start-placeholder` ID as a last resort

## How it works

The WordPress AI Client SDK calls `GET /webllm/v1/models` to discover available models. When the response `data` array is empty, the SDK throws `InvalidArgumentException` during capability matching — before any browser-side code (apiFetch middleware, SharedWorker idle-peek loop) can intervene to prompt the user to start the engine.

The placeholder model ID is never sent to the WebLLM engine. The SharedWorker's `autoPickModel()` selects the real model at load time, and `normaliseRequest()` overrides the `model` field with `currentModelId`. The existing cold-start infrastructure handles the rest:

1. **Browser path**: apiFetch middleware intercepts, calls `promptAndLoad()`, user sees the start modal
2. **Server loopback path**: broker enqueues the job, SharedWorker idle-peek detects `pending_jobs > 0`, broadcasts `needs-load`, widget auto-starts or shows modal

## Testing

1. Fresh install with no worker ever registered and no default model configured → SDK should no longer throw, should show the start modal instead
2. Default model configured but worker not yet started → SDK should pass capability matching using the configured default
3. Worker running with model loaded → no change in behaviour (hot path still returns the real model)

## Bug Fixes

When no active workers are available or registered, the system now defaults to the administrator-configured model. title: fix: add exponential backoff to idle polling loop and CI drift check (#32)
body:
## Summary

Addresses the two unresolved CodeRabbit findings from PR #26.

### 1. Exponential backoff in the idle polling loop (`src/worker.jsx`)

The `/jobs/next` polling loop had no delay on the idle path: a `204` response or an empty job payload caused it to immediately reissue the GET, hammering the server whenever the worker was online but had no work to do.

Now:
- `204` → sleep `retryDelay` (starts 1 s), then double up to 30 s cap
- no-job payload → same backoff
- real job received → reset `retryDelay` to 1 s
- HTTP error → reset `retryDelay` to 1 s (keeps the existing fixed 1 s delay)

This matches the CodeRabbit suggestion verbatim but implements full exponential backoff rather than a flat 1 s so sustained idle periods reduce to one poll per 30 s instead of one per second.

### 2. Build-drift CI check (`.github/workflows/build-drift.yml`)

New workflow runs on every PR and `main` push:
- `npm ci`
- `npm run build`
- `git diff --quiet --exit-code -- build/` → fails with an error message if `build/` has changed

This ensures committed bundles (`build/`) stay in sync with `src/` and prevents silent divergence of the WordPress Playground artifact.

## Testing

- `npm run build` ran cleanly (webpack 2 warnings — pre-existing entrypoint size notices, not new).
- Verified `Math.min(2*n,3e4)` appears twice in `build/worker.js` (204 path + no-job path) and the flat `1e3` delay remains on the error path.
- New CI workflow file validated against existing `release.yml` pattern.

Resolves #32

title: fix: include ONNX models in loadModel auto-pick candidate list
body:
## Summary

When `loadModel` is called without a `modelId`, the auto-pick fallback only fetched the WebLLM model list, so high-priority ONNX models (Gemma 4, Gemma 3) from the Transformers.js engine were never candidates for automatic selection — even though they appear correctly in the handshake response.

## Changes

**`src/shared-worker.js`**

1. **`loadModel` case** (lines 507-518): fetch both WebLLM and Transformers model lists in parallel via `Promise.all`, mirroring the pattern already used in the `handshake` case. ONNX models are prepended so they have positional priority before the sort.

2. **`autoPickModel` — `isChatModel` helper** (lines 180-186): WebLLM model IDs embed `instruct`/`chat` in the id string. ONNX models use `-it-` (instruction-tuned) in the id but carry `Instruct` in the human-readable `name` field. Without this companion fix, the freshly-fetched ONNX models would still be silently filtered out by the old `/instruct|chat/i.test(m.id)` check.

title: fix: ONNX models get priority in auto-pick — familyRank, isChatModel, dedup helper
body:
## Summary

Three fixes from CodeRabbit review of PR #46:

### 1. `familyRank` — ONNX families now win the primary sort (HIGH)

`familyRank` previously only matched WebLLM-style IDs (`Llama-3.2…Instruct`, `Qwen2.5…Instruct`, etc.), returning `0` for every ONNX model. The positional prepend (`[ ...tM, ...wM ]`) had no effect because even a Llama-3.2 build (rank 6) beat every ONNX model (rank 0). Added three new patterns ahead of the WebLLM tier:

| Pattern | Rank |
|---|---|
| `/gemma-4.*-it-ONNX/i` | 9 |
| `/gemma-3.*-it-ONNX/i` | 8 |
| `/Qwen3.*ONNX/i` | 7 |

### 2. `isChatModel` — Qwen3 0.6B no longer silently filtered (HIGH)

The `isChatModel(/instruct|chat/i)` check excluded `onnx-community/Qwen3-0.6B-ONNX` because its name was `'Qwen3 0.6B (ONNX)'` — no "instruct" or "chat". Renamed the `CURATED_MODELS` entry to `'Qwen3 0.6B Chat (ONNX)'` (consistent with the other ONNX entries: `'Gemma 4 E4B Instruct (ONNX)'`, etc.).

### 3. `getCombinedModelList()` helper — eliminates duplicate fetch code (nitpick)

The identical 5-line dual-engine fetch was duplicated verbatim in `handshake` and `loadModel`. Extracted into `getCombinedModelList()`. Also removes the misleading outer `try/catch` — `Promise.all` never rejects when both inner promises already have `.catch(() => [])`.

## Files changed

- `EDIT: src/shared-worker.js` — `familyRank` extension + `getCombinedModelList()` helper + both call sites updated
- `EDIT: src/transformers-engine.js` — Qwen3 0.6B name includes "Chat"

## Verification

1. `familyRank('onnx-community/gemma-4-E4B-it-ONNX')` → 9 (was 0)
2. `familyRank('onnx-community/Qwen3-0.6B-ONNX')` → 7 (was 0)
3. `isChatModel('onnx-community/Qwen3-0.6B-ONNX', 'Qwen3 0.6B Chat (ONNX)')` → true (was false)
4. `getCombinedModelList()` appears once in source; both call sites use it.

Resolves #47
